title: Ācta Diurna · Diēs Mercuriī, III Īd. Nov. (Wed 11 Nov 2026)
summary: Canberra: 9–28°, partly cloudy, afternoon storm chance; 11–27° and morning fog tomorrow; Brisbane storms, 31°. Australia: Albanese flies to COP31 in Turkey on a two-week trip; Taylor: 'this government has wrecked the economy'; Charlton backs Chalmers; Newspoll: One Nation 28%, Labor 27%. Iran: Trump: Iran 'militarily, is effectively over' but America is 'locked and loaded', another carrier heads east; Rezaei: 'surrender to Iran's seven conditions'. US: House votes on Massie's Hegseth impeachment resolution; Hegseth: 'a political spectacle'. Ukraine: Abu Dhabi talks open, first in nine months; Russia fired 162 drones overnight. Brisbane: rescuer frees a koala joey from a python. Opīniō: Rowan Dean, Trump fought Iran because it was right. St Martin of Tours; Armistice 1918. Every line in English, then Latin; then all the Latin again. Sources: Bureau of Meteorology; AAP (Canberra Times, Armidale Express, 10 Nov); The Nightly (10 Nov); Israel Hayom, The Week (10 Nov); Fox News (9–10 Nov); ANI (10 Nov); ABC News US (10 Nov); Kyiv Independent (10 Nov); Epoch Times (10 Nov); ABC News (6 Nov); The Spectator Australia (Rowan Dean, 9 Nov).
lines: spl
Hello, listeners. This is the Acta Diurna.
Salvēte, audītōrēs. Haec sunt Ācta Diurna.
pl
Today is Wednesday, the third day before the Ides of November.
Hodiē est diēs Mercuriī, ante diem tertium Īdūs Novembrēs.
pl
In the year 2026.
Annō bis mīllēsimō vīcēsimō sextō.
pl
First, the weather. Then Australian affairs.
Prīmum tempestās. Deinde rēs Austrāliae.
pl
Then the world: Iran, America, Ukraine.
Deinde orbis terrārum: Īrānia, America, Ūcraīna.
pl
Then a happy story, opinion, and today in history.
Tum rēs laeta, opīniō, et hodiē in historiā.
pl
At the end, the words of the day.
In fīne, verba diēī.
en
The weather. Canberra: partly cloudy and hot, 28 degrees, with perhaps a storm in the afternoon.
spl
The weather.
Tempestās.
pl
First, Canberra.
Prīmum Canberra.
pl
Yesterday we said: tomorrow 28 degrees, and in the afternoon perhaps thunder.
Herī dīximus: crās duodētrīgintā gradūs, et post merīdiem fortasse tonitrus.
pl
And so it is. Today in Canberra the sky is partly cloudy.
Et ita est. Hodiē Canberrae caelum partim nūbilum est.
pl
In the morning it is cool: 9 degrees.
Māne frīgidum est: novem gradūs.
pl
In the afternoon it is hot: 28 degrees.
Post merīdiem calidum est: duodētrīgintā gradūs.
pl
Perhaps a shower. In the afternoon perhaps thunder.
Fortasse imber. Post merīdiem fortasse tonitrus.
pl
At first the wind is light. In the evening it blows from the south-east, 15 to 20 kilometres an hour.
Prīmō ventus lēnis est. Vesperī ab austrō et oriente flat, quīndecim ad vīgintī chiliometra in hōrā.
pl
Tomorrow, Thursday, in the morning there may be fog.
Crās, diē Iovis, māne fortasse nebula erit.
pl
Then the sky will be partly cloudy.
Deinde caelum partim nūbilum erit.
pl
Tomorrow morning 11 degrees, in the afternoon 27.
Crās māne ūndecim gradūs, post merīdiem septem et vīgintī.
pl
Tomorrow too, in the afternoon, perhaps thunder.
Crās quoque, post merīdiem, fortasse tonitrus.
pl
So: today 28 degrees, tomorrow 27.
Ergō: hodiē duodētrīgintā gradūs, crās septem et vīgintī.
pl
Now the other cities.
Nunc cēterae urbēs.
pl
In Sydney perhaps thunder in the afternoon. 27 degrees.
Sydnēiae fortasse tonitrus post merīdiem. Septem et vīgintī gradūs.
pl
In Melbourne the sky is partly cloudy. 19 degrees.
Melburnī caelum partim nūbilum est. Ūndēvīgintī gradūs.
pl
In Brisbane storms are likely, perhaps fierce ones. 31 degrees.
Brisbanae tempestātēs probābilēs sunt, fortasse saevae. Ūnus et trīgintā gradūs.
pl
In Brisbane today it is hottest.
Brisbanae hodiē calidissimum est.
pl
In Perth the sun is shining. 28 degrees.
Perthī sōl lūcet. Duodētrīgintā gradūs.
pl
In Adelaide the sky is cloudy. 22 degrees.
Adēlāidae caelum nūbilum est. Duo et vīgintī gradūs.
pl
In Hobart the sky is partly cloudy. 21 degrees.
Hobartī caelum partim nūbilum est. Ūnus et vīgintī gradūs.
pl
That is the weather.
Haec est tempestās.
en
Australia. Albanese flies to the climate conference in Turkey, a new poll puts One Nation ahead of Labor, and Taylor says the government has wrecked the economy.
spl
Australian affairs.
Rēs Austrāliae.
pl
Yesterday we said: colleagues are leaking secrets against Chalmers.
Herī dīximus: collēgae sēcrēta contrā Chalmers prōdunt.
pl
And only one in five Australians trusts Albanese.
Et ūnus tantum ē quīnque Austrāliānīs Albanēsiō fidem habet.
pl
Yesterday Albanese flew to Turkey.
Herī Albanese in Turciam volāvit.
pl
In Turkey there is a great conference on the climate.
In Turciā est magnus conventus dē clīmate.
pl
Chris Bowen, the Australian minister, leads the talks at the conference.
Chris Bowen, minister Austrāliānus, sermōnēs in conventū dūcit.
pl
After Turkey, Albanese will fly to the Philippines and to China.
Post Turciam Albanese in Philippīnās et in Sīnās volābit.
pl
Albanese says: we must show leadership among the Pacific nations.
Albanese dīcit: prīncipātum apud gentēs Ōceanī Pācificī ostendere dēbēmus.
pl
But Angus Taylor, the leader of the Opposition, says:
Sed Angus Taylor, dux oppositiōnis, dīcit:
pl
The Prime Minister and this government have wrecked the economy.
Prīmus minister et haec rēs pūblica oeconomiam perdidērunt.
pl
The Prime Minister flies to Turkey; at home the economy is wrecked, as Taylor says.
Prīmus minister in Turciam volat; domī oeconomia perdita est, ut Taylor dīcit.
pl
But Bowen, in his speech, said nothing about energy prices.
Sed Bowen, in ōrātiōne suā, dē pretiīs energiae nihil dīxit.
pl
Now Chalmers.
Nunc Chalmers.
pl
Andrew Charlton, a minister, says: colleagues favour Chalmers.
Andreās Charlton, minister, dīcit: collēgae Chalmers favent.
pl
Because he is doing a good job, in difficult times.
Quia rem bene gerit, temporibus difficilibus.
pl
And Albanese says: my government is united.
Et Albanese dīcit: rēs pūblica mea concors est.
pl
And now a new poll, called Newspoll.
Et nunc nova percontātiō, quae Newspoll vocātur.
pl
27 per cent favour Labor.
Septem et vīgintī per centum Labōrānīs favent.
pl
But 28 per cent favour One Nation, the party of Pauline Hanson.
Sed duodētrīgintā per centum Ūnī Nātiōnī, factiōnī Paulīnae Hanson, favent.
pl
More Australians favour One Nation than Labor.
Plūrēs Austrāliānī Ūnī Nātiōnī favent quam Labōrānīs.
pl
The Prime Minister in Turkey, colleagues leaking secrets, fewer favouring Labor.
Prīmus minister in Turciā, collēgae sēcrēta prōdentēs, minus multī Labōrānīs faventēs.
pl
That is the state of Australia today.
Haec est rēs Austrāliae hodiē.
en
The world. Iran: Trump says the war is effectively over, but America is locked and loaded. Iran says: surrender to our seven conditions.
spl
The world.
Orbis terrārum.
pl
First, Iran.
Prīmum Īrānia.
pl
Yesterday we said: Trump says: Iron Gate is now in full force.
Herī dīximus: Trump dīcit: Porta Ferrea nunc plēnā vī agit.
pl
Today Trump says: Iron Gate is on land. So by land and by sea.
Hodiē Trump dīcit: Porta Ferrea in terrā est. Ergō terrā et marī.
pl
And Trump says: the war with Iran is effectively over.
Et Trump dīcit: bellum cum Īrāniā paene cōnfectum est.
pl
We are only keeping things as they are.
Rēs tantum servāmus ut sunt.
pl
But if we must go back, we are ready.
Sed sī redīre dēbēmus, parātī sumus.
pl
And another great ship, which carries aeroplanes, is coming to the East.
Et alia nāvis magna, quae āeroplana portat, ad Orientem venit.
pl
The blockade remains, by land and by sea.
Obsidiō manet, terrā et marī.
pl
Yesterday we said: Iran still demands seven conditions.
Herī dīximus: Īrānia adhūc septem condiciōnēs postulat.
pl
Today Mohsen Rezaei, a leader in Iran, says: it is time to give in to Iran's seven conditions.
Hodiē Mohsen Rezaei, prīnceps Īrāniae, dīcit: tempus est septem condiciōnibus Īrāniae cēdere.
pl
Among them: an end to the blockade and an end to sanctions.
Inter eās: fīnem obsidiōnis et fīnem poenārum.
pl
But Trump says: the Iranians are talking to us, and they are talking very well.
Sed Trump dīcit: Īrāniī nōbīscum loquuntur, et valdē bene loquuntur.
pl
And the price of oil fell, by almost 7 per cent.
Et pretium oleī cecidit, paene septem per centum.
pl
The war is effectively over, but America is ready.
Bellum paene cōnfectum est, sed America parāta est.
en
America. Today, American time, the House votes on Massie's plan to impeach Hegseth. Hegseth calls it a political spectacle.
pl
Now the United States of America.
Nunc Cīvitātēs Foederātae Americae.
pl
Yesterday we said: perhaps this very week the House of Representatives will vote on Hegseth.
Herī dīximus: fortasse hāc ipsā hebdomade Domus Repraesentantium dē Hegseth suffrāgium feret.
pl
Today Thomas Massie says: today the House will vote.
Hodiē Thomas Massie dīcit: hodiē Domus suffrāgium feret.
pl
Massie has written eight charges against Hegseth, the Secretary of War.
Massie octō crīmina contrā Hegseth, ministrum bellī, scrīpsit.
pl
The first charge: war in Iran without the consent of Congress.
Prīmum crīmen: bellum in Īrāniā sine cōnsēnsū Congressūs.
pl
But first the House will vote: should the plan be killed?
Sed prīmum Domus suffrāgium feret: dēbetne cōnsilium exstinguī?
pl
Hegseth says: this is a political spectacle.
Hegseth dīcit: hoc est spectāculum polīticum.
pl
A spectacle born of pride and resentment.
Spectāculum ex superbiā et invidiā nātum.
pl
And Trump defends Hegseth. Trump says: Hegseth has won the war in Iran.
Et Trump Hegseth dēfendit. Trump dīcit: Hegseth bellum in Īrāniā vīcit.
pl
In Mississippi postal votes are no longer accepted. The count goes on.
In Mississippiā epistulae cum suffrāgiīs iam nōn accipiuntur. Numerātiō pergit.
pl
The Senate seat in Mississippi is still undecided.
Sēdēs senātūs in Mississippiā adhūc incerta est.
en
Ukraine. The talks in Abu Dhabi have begun, the first in nine months. Russia sent 162 drones the night before.
pl
Now Ukraine.
Nunc Ūcraīna.
pl
Yesterday we said: today the talks on peace begin in the city of Abu Dhabi.
Herī dīximus: hodiē sermōnēs dē pāce in urbe Abu Dhabi incipiunt.
pl
And so it is. The talks have begun.
Et ita est. Sermōnēs coepērunt.
pl
They are the first talks in nine months.
Prīmī sermōnēs sunt post novem mēnsēs.
pl
The Americans lead the talks: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Americānī sermōnēs dūcunt: Stephanus Witkoff et Iared Kushner.
pl
Rustem Umerov leads the Ukrainians. Vladimir Medinsky leads the Russians.
Rustem Umerov Ūcraīnōs dūcit. Vladimīrus Medinsky Russōs dūcit.
pl
The Ukrainians want a ceasefire first.
Ūcraīnī prīmum indūtiās volunt.
pl
A ceasefire at sea, and a ceasefire for the power stations.
Indūtiās in marī, et indūtiās prō stātiōnibus ēlectricīs.
pl
But the Russians demand that the Ukrainians leave the Donbas.
Sed Russī postulant ut Ūcraīnī ex Donbassō discēdant.
pl
And before the talks the Russians attacked again.
Et ante sermōnēs Russī iterum oppugnāvērunt.
pl
In one night the Russians sent 162 drones and one missile.
Ūnā nocte Russī centum sexāgintā duōs fūcōs et ūnum missile mīsērunt.
pl
The Ukrainians brought down 135 drones.
Ūcraīnī centum trīgintā quīnque fūcōs dēiēcērunt.
pl
Trump says: the war is going to end, and it is going to end soon.
Trump dīcit: bellum fīniētur, et mox fīniētur.
pl
Talks in the city of Abu Dhabi, drones in the night, and the war goes on.
Sermōnēs in urbe Abu Dhabi, fūcī noctū, et bellum pergit.
en
Something good. In Brisbane a woman freed a baby koala from a python and gave it back to its mother.
spl
Good news.
Rēs laeta.
pl
In Brisbane there is a woman named Nell. She rescues animals.
Brisbanae est fēmina, nōmine Nell. Animālia servat.
pl
Nell was walking with her dog, Pluto, in a park.
Nell cum cane suō, Plūtōne, in hortō pūblicō ambulābat.
pl
Suddenly she saw a snake. The snake was a python, about one and a half metres long.
Subitō serpentem vīdit. Serpēns pȳthōn erat, circiter ūnum metrum et dīmidium longus.
pl
The snake was holding a baby koala tight.
Serpēns īnfantem koālam artē tenēbat.
pl
The mother koala was trying to pull the snake away.
Māter koāla serpentem dētrahere cōnābātur.
pl
Nell freed the baby koala. It had no wound.
Nell īnfantem koālam līberāvit. Nūllum vulnus habēbat.
pl
She gave the baby back to its mother.
Īnfantem mātrī reddidit.
pl
Nell says: an hour or two later, I saw the mother and her baby hugging.
Nell dīcit: ūnā aut duābus hōrīs post, mātrem et īnfantem sē amplectentēs vīdī.
pl
And they looked so happy.
Et tam laetae vidēbantur.
pl
A small koala, a great work.
Parva koāla, magnum opus.
en
Opinion. This is the view of Rowan Dean, in The Spectator Australia: Trump went to war with Iran because it was right, not to be popular.
spl
Opinion.
Opīniō.
pl
This is the view of Rowan Dean, in The Spectator Australia.
Haec est sententia Rowan Dean, in Spectātōre Austrāliānō.
pl
Yesterday we said: Vance says: the reason we lost is the war.
Herī dīximus: Vance dīcit: causa clādis nostrae est bellum.
pl
Dean agrees: the war with Iran cost the Republicans the elections.
Dean cōnsentit: bellum cum Īrāniā Rēpūblicānīs comitia abstulit.
pl
But Dean says: Trump began the war with Iran because it was right.
Sed Dean dīcit: Trump bellum cum Īrāniā coepit quia rēctum erat.
pl
Not to be popular.
Nōn ut populō placēret.
pl
Dean says: Vance wanted a ceasefire and talks with Iran.
Dean dīcit: Vance indūtiās et sermōnēs cum Īrāniā voluit.
pl
But the ceasefire in April made Iran's regime stronger, as Dean says.
Sed indūtiae mēnse Aprīlī imperium Īrāniae cōnfirmāvērunt, ut Dean dīcit.
pl
Now there are only two ways: either Iran's regime falls, or Iran defeats Israel and the West.
Nunc duae tantum viae sunt: aut imperium Īrāniae cadit, aut Īrānia Isrāēlem et Occidentem vincit.
pl
Dean also criticises Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly and Candace Owens, who turned against Trump.
Dean etiam Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly, et Candace Owens reprehendit, quī contrā Trump versī sunt.
pl
Some of their words, as Dean says, crossed into hatred of Jews.
Quaedam verba eōrum, ut Dean dīcit, in odium Iūdaeōrum trānsiērunt.
pl
That is the opinion of Rowan Dean.
Haec est opīniō Rowan Dean.
en
On this day the Church keeps the feast of Saint Martin of Tours, the Roman soldier who cut his cloak in half for a beggar. And today is Remembrance Day.
spl
Today in history.
Hodiē in historiā.
pl
Today the Church celebrates the feast of Saint Martin.
Hodiē Ecclēsia fēstum sānctī Mārtīnī celebrat.
pl
Martin was born in Pannonia, about the year 316.
Mārtīnus in Pannoniā nātus est, circiter annō trecentēsimō sextō decimō.
pl
He was a Roman soldier, a horseman.
Mīles Rōmānus erat, eques.
pl
In the city of Amiens he saw a beggar.
In urbe Ambiānōrum mendīcum vīdit.
pl
Martin cut his cloak in two with his sword, and gave half to the beggar.
Mārtīnus pallium suum gladiō in duās partēs dīvīsit, et dīmidium mendīcō dedit.
pl
At night he saw Christ in a dream, wearing the half cloak.
Noctū Chrīstum in somnō vīdit, dīmidium pallium gerentem.
pl
Later Martin became bishop of Tours.
Posteā Mārtīnus episcopus Turonum factus est.
pl
He died in the year 397, and on this day, the 11th of November, he was buried in Tours.
Annō trecentēsimō nōnāgēsimō septimō mortuus est, et hodiē, diē ūndecimō Novembris, Turonibus sepultus est.
pl
And today, in the year 1918, at the eleventh hour, an armistice was made, and the Great War ended.
Et hodiē, annō mīllēsimō nōngentēsimō duodēvīcēsimō, hōrā ūndecimā, indūtiae factae sunt, et Bellum Magnum fīnītum est.
pl
Today in Australia, at the eleventh hour, we remember the fallen soldiers.
Hodiē in Austrāliā, hōrā ūndecimā, mīlitum mortuōrum meminimus.
pl
Marcus and Lucius, as always, were there. But that is another story.
Mārcus et Lūcius, ut semper, aderant. Sed id alia fābula est.
en

Brisbanae Nell īnfantem koālam ā serpente līberāvit.

Today is the feast of Saint Martin, bishop of Tours.
Hodiē est fēstum sānctī Mārtīnī, episcopī Turonum.
